description: The WorldRiskIndex is a statistical model that assesses the latent risk of 193 countries suffering a humanitarian disaster from extreme natural events and the negative impacts of climate change. It treats exposure and vulnerability as equal spheres of disaster risk, on the view that social, political and economic conditions shape disasters as much as the hazards themselves. It was first developed in 2011 by the United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security for Bündnis Entwicklung Hilft with 27 indicators, has been revised by the IFHV since 2018, and in 2022 was replaced by a fully revised model with more than 100 indicators, new data sources and more robust statistics. IFHV publishes trend data and archives on the Humanitarian Data Exchange, covering 2000 to the present and updated yearly, as downloadable CSV and GeoPackage files with a metadata workbook, a special exposure archive and a legacy data archive, under CC BY. Caveats: conflicts, wars and pandemics are deliberately considered only partly or not at all, results are national aggregates, and legacy archive scores come from the earlier 27-indicator model. It is useful for country-level hazard exposure and social vulnerability screening, prioritising resilience investment and scenario context for climate adaptation; a related record is the CDC Social Vulnerability Index.
